title: Breitspur 01
subtitle: 1972 BMW 2002
summary: Round tails, riveted Turbo flares, multipiece mesh wheels and a pink tow strap for Ruxin.
thesis: Breitspur's first concept car: a 1972 BMW 2002 drawn as the Turbo prototype that never was.  Round taillights and kidney grilles untouched, riveted flares, multipiece mesh wheels and a cage, and a set of quiet tributes to a small, fast dog named Ruxin.

photo.alt: Close detail of the 2002's front corner: riveted fender flare, polished mesh wheel, black grille and raw aluminum splitter with tow strap

parts.name: Black Anodized Early Grilles
parts.note: The all black side grilles in the render, made from the early aluminum grilles your car already has.  Have them anodized black, so the color is part of the metal and cannot peel.
parts.fitment: Ask the shop for electrolytic (two step) black, which holds up in the sun better than dyed black, and a sealed finish; expect a satin result.  Remove the plastic reflectors and hardware first, and have the shop inspect the grilles before you commit.  To keep your originals, anodize a new set instead.
parts.priceNote: Anodizing is a local shop quote.  New early grille set with kidney, $1,250, linked here

also.label: 1974 or later car? Black plastic grilles bolt on, Mecatechnic

parts.name: Ground Control Complete Suspension
parts.note: Koni adjustable inserts, threaded perches and camber plates, built on your own strut housings.  Owners run this kit at zero fender gap, the height in these renders, and still drive their cars.
parts.fitment: Ground Control builds the kit on your bare strut housings, so you send those in.  Set final height with your wheels and flares fitted, so the tires clear the arches under compression.

also.label: Budget path: Bilstein Sport struts and shocks, $702
Pair with H&R Sport springs, 1.25 in drop, $339.99
See owner cars on Ground Control, 2002FAQ forum

parts.name: Turbo Style Fender Flares
parts.note: Set of four in black ABS, shaped after the 2002 Turbo.  Trim the arch lip, then rivet them on for the look in the render.

parts.name: BBS RS Three Piece, Staggered
parts.note: The riveted mesh wheel in the renders: BBS RS centers rebuilt with new lips to any width and offset.  Spec it staggered, 15 x 7 in front and 15 x 8 in back.
parts.fitment: Targets are about ET10 to ET15 in front and about ET0 in back.  Test fit one wheel with the flares on and the car at ride height before the set is built.  Budget path: the Vors VR3 has the same cross mesh, riveted ring and stepped lip in a one piece wheel and the same two sizes, but sits about 20 mm inboard.  Add 20 mm hub centric spacers at all four corners with longer studs, get at least 8 full turns on every lug nut, and fit hub rings from its 73.1 mm bore down to the 2002's 57.1 mm.
parts.priceNote: A restored 15 x 7 set lists at $5,000.  A staggered build is quoted to order

also.label: Building it yourself? New 15 in RS step lips, WheelFlip, $227 each
Budget path: Vors VR3 mesh, 15 x 7 ET32 front and 15 x 8 ET20 rear, $165 each
With the VR3: 20 mm hub centric spacers, Ireland Engineering, $68 a pair

parts.name: Kumho Ecsta V730, Staggered
parts.note: The one 200 treadwear street tire made in both sizes the wheels need: 205/50R15 front and 225/45R15 rear.  A warm weather tire, so leave the car parked on a cold snap.
parts.fitment: Kumho says not to drive or store it near freezing, so it suits warm climates year round and colder ones from spring through fall.  The 225/45 rear is the right size for the 8 in rim, and the two sizes are within half a percent in diameter.  Grooved for rain, but slow down in a downpour.

also.label: Track days only: Toyo Proxes R888R 225/45R15, about $197 each; grippy when hot, poor in rain and cold

parts.name: KoogleWerks Wide Aluminum Air Dam
parts.note: A hand made aluminum air dam that wraps around to the wheel arch lip and can stay raw like the render.  Order the high mount, long, no bumper version.
parts.fitment: High mount is KoogleWerks' pick for a lowered car, and the wide version takes more fitting skill, since every car is a little different.  It ships with stainless bolts and no holes drilled; swap in rivets or button head bolts for the exposed rivet look.  At this ride height it is the lowest point on the car, so expect to scrape it on steep driveways.
parts.priceNote: In stock, ships in a wooden crate

also.label: Budget path: IE flexible air dam, $195, plus a home made aluminum blade

parts.name: Supersprint Muffler, Dual 60 mm Tips
parts.note: Rear muffler with twin tips, listed for the 1602, 2002 and 2002tii.  Gives the M10 a real voice without drone.

parts.name: AST Removable Rear Cage
parts.note: A rear half cage built for the 2002 coupe, with no door bars, so getting in stays easy.  It unbolts whenever you want it out once its mounting plates are welded in.
parts.fitment: 45 mm main hoop and 40 mm bracing on four 3 mm steel plates welded to the body, so plan on a welder or a shop for that one step.  AST says it is built for road use and does not claim homologation, so it is not a substitute for a full cage on track.
parts.priceNote: €534 before Spanish VAT, €646 with it.  Made to order in 15 to 35 working days, then ships from Spain

also.label: No welding: IE bolt in roll bar with diagonal and harness bar, $950
Track spec: Sparco FIA 6 point bolt in cage, about $1,680, confirm fit first

parts.name: MOMO Prototipo Black, 350 mm
parts.note: Black leather rim and black anodized spokes with drilled holes, the wheel in the cabin render.  It mounts with MOMO's 1600 to 2002 hub adapter; both are listed here.

parts.name: Recaro Classic LS, Black Leather
parts.note: Recaro's own reissue of its 1984 LS sport seat, in black leather, reclining, made in Germany.  Each seat mounts on KoogleWerks brackets that use the stock BMW sliders.
parts.fitment: The brackets sit the seat as low as possible, one set per seat; confirm they suit the Classic LS with KoogleWerks before ordering.
parts.priceNote: Two seats at $2,495, two bracket sets at $100

shops.label: Seat brackets, one set per seat

also.label: Second option: vintage Recaros restored and recovered by Aardvarc, about $900 to $1,300 a set when in stock

parts.name: Lathe Werks Stainless Sphere Knob
parts.note: A 2 in solid stainless ball in torched bronze, the warm metal knob in the render.  Made to order in 7 to 14 days.
parts.fitment: About 1 lb, screwing on with a brass insert and set screws.  Lathe Werks does not list the 2002's shifter thread, so confirm fit when you order.

parts.name: Turner Aluminum Pedal Set, Manual
parts.note: CNC machined aluminum pads, with grip spikes on clutch and brake and a smoother throttle for heel and toe.  Made in the USA, with a drilling template and stainless hardware.

bundle.name: Stance Kit
bundle.pitch: The four parts that make this look, in install order: get it low, give it room, fill the arches, then put the right rubber under them.

detailing.note: Wash, then clay.  Fifty year old single stage paint holds grime the mitt leaves behind.
Black single stage paint shows every swirl.  A gentle polish brings back the depth.  Expect black on the pad; that is the paint, and it is normal.
Spray on, wipe off.  Ten minutes for months of gloss and water beading.

designerNote: Car companies build these raw, emotional things that never get to see the streets.  I want people to actually get to experience them.

conceptNote: The Breitspur 01 is a concept render, not a finished car.  Every part below is a real, off the shelf part, listed in install order, so you can build the attainable version of this look yourself.
deck: Breitspur's first concept car is a BMW 2002 that hits harder than it looks, and it is a tribute to a small, fast dog named Ruxin.  We talked with Nick DiLoreto, design director and principal of Breitspur, about what went into it.

article.label: The brief
article.heading: What was off limits when you started sketching?
body: The car is extremely iconic, so the round taillights and the kidney grilles were never up for discussion.  What I wanted was a beefier take on it.  A true tribute, something that could have been the prototype for the 2002 Turbo.
article.caption: Side profile.  The shape is untouched; everything sits lower and wider.

article.label: The tribute
article.heading: Who is Ruxin, and where does he show up in the car?
body: This build was a creative outlet for me after my dog Ruxin died, and the whole car is a tribute to him.  The tow straps are pink, not red, because they're meant to look like his little pink tongue.  He was a black dog with white on him, so the black, silver, and white palette comes from him.

He loved the ocean and the beach and anything with water, and that's the blue in the door cards.  He was also a very athletic little dog, always the fastest one at the dog park.  Small and fast, just like the car.
article.caption: Pink, not red.  The tow straps are for Ruxin.

article.label: The stance
article.heading: How do you make a 2002 look muscular without losing what makes it delicate?
body: Mostly with the flared arches and the multipiece wheels.  They give it that wide, low character I was after.  The centered rear exhaust makes the car look wider too, and it plays off the round taillights.
article.caption: Riveted flare, multipiece mesh wheel and the raw aluminum splitter.

article.label: The why
article.heading: Where does the urge to build something this raw come from?
body: When I was a young designer at Volvo I got to drive a prototype S40 they never did anything with.  It was raw, loud, and had loads of power, a monster.  I always found it a bit sad that car companies build these raw, emotional machines and the public never gets to see them.

I know a car that loud probably would have struggled with mass buyers, but there was something so cool about it.  For me, a huge part of all this is building those kinds of cars and letting people actually experience them.  That's what I tried to get across with the 01.
article.caption: Round tails, Turbo flares and the cage through the glass.

article.label: The driver
article.heading: Who is the 01 for?
body: It's a weekend car, not a daily driver.  It's stiff, it's loud, it's raw.  It's the thing you look forward to on Saturday morning, the car you grab when you want that adrenaline hit out on the backcountry roads.

article.label: The status
article.heading: Is it built?
body: Not yet, and I want to be upfront about that.  The 01 is our first concept car, and we hope to build it soon.

article.label: The last word
article.heading: What would Ruxin make of it?
body: He loved car rides.  When he was a puppy I had a Volkswagen GTI, and we'd take it to the park, the ocean, the lake.  There was nothing better than his face looking up at me from the passenger footwell, because he knew we were off to do something fun.  I think he'd connect this car with those same good things.
article.caption: Blue door cards, for a dog who loved the water.

article.label: Before you buy
article.heading: What we would tell a friend
body: Do not swap the nose to get black grilles.  Early cars, through August 1973, keep their own aluminum grilles; have them anodized black so the finish cannot peel.  The black plastic grilles bolt straight on only if your car is a 1974 or later.  The flares need the arch lip trimmed.  The blue pleated door cards, the black dash and the warm gauge faces are trim shop work, not parts: take the cabin render to an upholsterer.  The cage is made to order in Spain, 15 to 35 working days before it ships, so order it first, and line up a welder for its mounting plates before it arrives.
